text: {"frames":["Your hand is already on the frame when the painted sailor's arm drops, so you pull the portrait off the wall before he can climb out. Behind it the corridor smells of warm milk and pepper, and the dream seller, Juffrouw Bekker, sits on a stool stoppering jars of dreams with shaking fingers. 'He stepped into the canal in the picture and his boat is sinking,' she whispers. The sailor waves at you from the painted water, and above his head a small clock in the picture has stopped with its glass cracked. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","Imogen the lock keeper has her shoulder against the gate and her eyes on the barge stuck below. The water in the lock rises and falls, rises and falls, as if it is breathing in its sleep, and every breath lifts the barge a finger's width and drops it back. 'Not one moment longer than the ice allows,' she mutters, and she taps the big clock in the picture on the lock house wall with her pipe. The hands of that clock have a mind of their own, but its face is clear enough for anyone who looks. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","A smell of hot waffles and tar comes up the stairwell, and you climb toward it on a staircase that is not on the plan of the Tower. Sjaak, the cheese maker's apprentice, sits on the top step and grins at you with a wheel of cheese on his knees. 'Bet you a herring you cannot find the floor that isn't there,' he says, and he points at the wall, where a clock in the picture hangs beside a windmill painted in blue. Its hands are the only honest thing on this landing, so trust them. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","Fenna, the learned owl from the mill, lifts her spectacles with one wing and tells you to blow out your lamp at once. The blue lantern on the barge across the canal is burning, and it is bobbing toward the stairs as if it wants to be followed. 'Do not follow the light, follow the clock,' she says, and she taps the clock in the picture on the mill wall with her beak. Its brass face is spotless and its hands point clearly at the time. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits.","The canal has run backwards again in the night, and Briony the talking stork stands on the wrong bank with a tulip in her beak. 'Everything here is upside down, the boats, the cheese, the tide,' she sighs, and she points her beak at the clock in the picture on the windmill's sail. The clock is painted onto the canvas, but someone has drawn its hands in fresh green paint, and they are dripping. What time does the clock in the picture show? Write the time with digits."]}
